definition_zh: 历史上；从历史角度；在过去；按历史顺序
definition_en: in relation to history or the past, or in a way that follows the order of past events
core_image: 一条从左向右延伸的时间轴，轴上每隔一段有一个小旗
scene: 这里指「历史上」。 Historically, the river has flooded every spring, though dikes now prevent it.
sceneCN: 这里 historically 是「历史上」（第 1 个义项：在过去的事实中一贯如此）；句意：历史上这条河每年春天都会泛滥，尽管如今堤坝已能阻止它。图中可辨识物件：时间轴、小旗、河流、堤坝、旧照片。

senses.title: In the recorded past
senses.titleCN: 历史上：在有记载的过去一直如此
senses.definition: in the past as recorded, especially as a long-standing pattern
senses.definitionCN: 在有记录的过去，尤指作为一种长期存在的模式
senses.example: Historically, the valley has produced more apples than grain.
senses.exampleCN: 历史上，这条谷地产的苹果一直多于谷物。
senses.why: history comes from Greek historia 'inquiry, account'; historically marks what belongs to the recorded account of the past.
senses.whyCN: history 出自希腊 historia“探究、记述”；historically 标记属于过去之记载的事物。

senses.title: Seen from history's angle
senses.titleCN: 从历史角度看：把长时段作为参照
senses.definition: when judged over a long span rather than from the present moment alone
senses.definitionCN: 以长时段而非仅以当下为参照来判断
senses.example: Historically, the two countries have traded more than they have fought.
senses.exampleCN: 从历史角度看，这两国贸易多于交战。
senses.why: The adverb can frame a judgement rather than state a fact, putting the whole record in view.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词可以框定一次判断而非陈述一个事实，把整部记录纳入视野。

senses.title: In the past, not now
senses.titleCN: 在过去：曾经如此，如今已不同
senses.definition: formerly, implying that the situation has since changed
senses.definitionCN: 过去曾经，暗含此后情况已经改变
senses.example: Historically, women were barred from this profession; today they are the majority.
senses.exampleCN: 过去女性被排斥在这一行业之外，如今她们占多数。
senses.why: When the adverb contrasts with now, it marks a boundary in time; the sentence carries an implicit 'but not anymore'.
senses.whyCN: 当这个副词与“现在”形成对照时，它标记一道时间界线，句子便暗含“如今不再如此”。

senses.title: In order of events
senses.titleCN: 按历史顺序：依时间先后排列
senses.definition: arranged or narrated in the order in which events occurred
senses.definitionCN: 按事件发生的先后次序排列或叙述
senses.example: The chapters are organized historically, from settlement to industrialization.
senses.exampleCN: 各章按历史顺序组织，从定居到工业化。
senses.why: History is also a sequence; the adverb can mark chronology rather than a judgement about the past.
senses.whyCN: 历史同时也是一条序列；这个副词可以标记年代次序，而非对过去的判断。

senses.title: As history is practised
senses.titleCN: 史学上：就史料与考据而言
senses.definition: in terms of historical method, evidence and scholarship
senses.definitionCN: 就历史学的方法、证据与学术规范而言
senses.example: Historically, the account rests on two letters and no continuous record.
senses.exampleCN: 就史学而言，这一叙述只建立在两封信上，没有连续记录。
senses.why: The adverb can point at the discipline's standards rather than at past time itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词可以指向学科标准，而非过去的时间本身。

senses.title: By long tradition
senses.definition: according to a long-established practice handed down over time
senses.definitionCN: 依照长期沿袭、世代相传的做法
senses.example: Historically, the land was held in common rather than owned.
senses.exampleCN: 传统上，这片土地是共有的，而非私有的。
senses.why: Long usage is history in its practical form, so the adverb often means little more than 'as has long been done'.
senses.whyCN: 长期的惯用是历史在实践中的形态，因此这个副词常只表示“按长期以来的做法”。

senses.title: Measured against past levels
senses.titleCN: 按历史标准看：与过去水平相比
senses.definition: compared with the range of values recorded in earlier periods
senses.definitionCN: 与更早时期记录到的数值范围相比较
senses.example: Rainfall this year is historically low for the region.
senses.exampleCN: 今年的降雨量对该地区而言处于历史低位。
senses.why: Statistics needs a baseline, and history supplies it; the adverb marks the comparison that makes 'low' or 'high' meaningful.
senses.whyCN: 统计需要一个基线，而历史提供基线；这个副词标记的正是使“低”或“高”有意义的比较。

senses.title: Within its own period
senses.titleCN: 在历史脉络中：结合时代背景来看
senses.definition: understood within the conditions and ideas of its own period
senses.definitionCN: 在其所处时代的环境与观念中加以理解
senses.example: The decision must be read historically, not judged only by today's values.
senses.exampleCN: 这一决定必须放在历史脉络中解读，而不能只用今天的价值标准来评判。
senses.why: This sense asks the reader to enter a past context, the most methodological use of the adverb.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项要求读者进入过去的语境，是这个副词最具方法论色彩的一种用法。

intro.en: Historically is historical plus -ly. The base is Greek historia 'inquiry, account', through Latin historia and Old French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: historically 是 historical 加 -ly。词基为希腊 historia“探究、记述”，经拉丁 historia 与古法语传入。年代为约数。

items.en: historia meant 'inquiry, investigation, a written account of findings'. It came from histōr 'witness, one who knows', a word of uncertain deeper origin.
items.cn: historia 意为“探究、调查、对发现的书面记述”，出自 histōr“见证者、知情者”，该词更深来源不确定。

items.en: Herodotus used historia in the 5th century BC for his inquiry into the Persian wars, and the word became tied to ordered narration of events.
items.cn: 公元前 5 世纪，希罗多德用 historia 指他对波斯战争的探究，此词由此与对事件的有序叙述绑定。

items.en: Latin historia meant both 'narrative' and 'the knowing of events'. Old French estoire produced English history in the 13th century; story is a doublet from the same source.
items.cn: 拉丁 historia 兼指“叙述”与“对事件的了解”。古法语 estoire 于 13 世纪产生英语 history；story 是同源的双重借词。

items.en: historical is recorded in the 16th century, and historically follows as its adverb, first in the sense 'according to history'.
items.cn: historical 于 16 世纪有记录，historically 作为其副词随后出现，最初意为“依照历史”。

items.en: In the 20th century historically low and historically high became common in economics and climate writing, where history means the recorded series.
items.cn: 20 世纪，historically low 与 historically high 在经济与气候写作中普及，其中 history 指记录下来的数据序列。

items.en: The origin of Greek histōr is disputed, and the exact date of the first English use of historically is uncertain.
items.cn: 希腊 histōr 的来源有争议；historically 在英语中首次使用的确切年代存疑。

note.en: The first group contains words that are easily swapped with this adverb; the second contains adverbs of time and tradition.
note.cn: 第一组是易与本副词互换的词；第二组是表示时间与传统的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective. Use it before nouns or after linking verbs; use historically to modify an action or a whole judgement.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词；置于名词前或系动词后；修饰动作或整体判断时应用 historically。

entries.definition: Meaning 'important in history, momentous'. A historic decision is one that will be remembered; a historical decision is merely one made in the past.
entries.definitionCN: 意为“在历史上重要的、有重大意义的”。historic decision 指将被记住的决定；historical decision 只指过去作出的决定。

entries.definition: From histrio 'actor', meaning 'in an exaggerated theatrical way'. It sounds close to historically but is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 histrio“演员”，意为“以夸张做作的方式”；读音接近 historically，但词源无关。

entries.definition: According to long-established custom; it stresses transmission, while historically stresses the record.
entries.definitionCN: 依照长期形成的习俗；强调传承，而 historically 强调记录。

entries.definition: In earlier times, with a clear contrast to now; it lacks the long-record implication of historically.
entries.definitionCN: 在较早时期，与现在形成明确对照；不含 historically 那种“长期记录”的意味。

entries.definition: In order of dates; it covers sense 4 precisely and says nothing about importance or tradition.
entries.definitionCN: 按日期次序；精确对应第 4 个义项，不涉及重要性或传统。

entries.definition: A plain phrase for earlier time; it is vaguer than historically about how far back and how well recorded.
entries.definitionCN: 指较早时间的普通说法；在“多久以前”和“记录多完整”上比 historically 更含糊。

entries.definition: Across a period, without implying records or scholarship; it focuses on gradual development.
entries.definitionCN: 在一段时期内；不暗示记录或学术，而着眼于逐渐发展。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: historical + -ly: in the manner of history.
normal.cn: historical + -ly：以历史的方式。

normal.en: historically low, historically high and historically speaking are the commonest frames.
normal.cn: historically low、historically high、historically speaking 是最常见的框架。

normal.en: The family is history, historical, historic, historian, historically.
normal.cn: 同族词是 history、historical、historic、historian、historically。

normal.en: historically goes with historical, not with historic; keep the pair apart.
normal.cn: historically 对应的是 historical 而非 historic；这一对要分清。

normal.en: A sentence with historically usually implies a long record behind the statement.
normal.cn: 含 historically 的句子通常暗示该陈述背后有长期记录。

abstract.en: Picture a timeline with small flags at every flood, each flag adding to a pattern.
abstract.cn: 想象一条时间轴，每次洪水处插一面小旗，旗子累积成一个规律。

abstract.en: Picture a graph line stretching back a century so that today's point can be called low.
abstract.cn: 想象一条延伸百年的曲线，今次的点才能被称为低位。

abstract.en: Picture a reader stepping through a doorway into the ideas of another century.
abstract.cn: 想象读者穿过一道门，走进另一个世纪的观念之中。

examples.en: Historically, the region depended on one crop, and a single bad harvest could empty every store.
examples.cn: 历史上，该地区依赖单一作物，一次歉收就能掏空所有粮仓。

examples.en: Housing costs are historically high relative to local wages.
examples.cn: 相对于当地工资，住房成本处于历史高位。

examples.en: The building was listed historically important, though it is only eighty years old.
examples.cn: 这座建筑被列为具有历史重要性，尽管它只有八十年历史。

dict_mnemonic.text: “history（历史）+ ally（地）”——以历史为伴地看问题 → historically 历史上、从历史角度

root: 希腊 historia“探究、记述”← histōr“见证者”；拉丁 historia、古法语 estoire → 英语 history + -ical + -ly。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all point backward, but in different ways: as a record, as a long span, as a contrast with now, as a sequence, as a method and as a baseline.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都指向后方，但方式各异：作为记录、作为长时段、作为与现在的对照、作为序列、作为方法，以及作为基线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a timeline running left to right, flagged at each past event.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条自左向右延伸的时间轴，每个过去事件处插着一面旗。

branches.en: RECORD AND TRADITION: what has been recorded and what has long been done are two forms of the same backward look.
branches.cn: 记录与传统：被记录下来的与长期沿袭的，是同一种回望的两种形态。

branches.en: THE LONG VIEW: judging over a span and reading within a past context both widen the frame.
branches.cn: 长视：以长时段作判断、在过去语境中阅读，都是把框架放宽。

branches.en: THEN AND NOW: the adverb can mark the moment when a former practice ended.
branches.cn: 彼时与此时：这个副词可以标记某一旧做法终止的时刻。

branches.en: ORDER AND METHOD: chronology and scholarship are the discipline's two working tools.
branches.cn: 次序与方法：年代排序与学术考据，是这门学科的两件工具。

branches.en: BASELINE: 'low' or 'high' only means something against the recorded series.
branches.cn: 基线：“低”或“高”只有在与记录序列相比时才有意义。

intro.en: Historically is history plus -ical plus -ly, all inherited through Latin and French from Greek historia.
intro.cn: historically 是 history 加 -ical 再加 -ly，整体经拉丁与法语传承自希腊 historia。

latinIntro.en: The historia family includes history, story, historical, historic, historian, historiography and the unrelated histrionic, which comes from a different Latin word for actor.
latinIntro.cn: historia 词族包括 history、story、historical、historic、historian、historiography，以及词源无关的 histrionic（出自另一个表示演员的拉丁词）。

items.meaning: in terms of history or the past
items.example: Historically, the two families shared the water.
items.exampleCN: 历史上，这两家共用这份水源。

items.example: The archive holds the historical records of the port.
items.exampleCN: 档案馆保存着该港口的历史记录。

items.example: The treaty was a historic achievement.
items.exampleCN: 这项条约是一项历史性成就。

items.meaning: the recorded past, or the study of it
items.meaningCN: 被记录的过去，或对它的研究
items.example: History is written from the documents that survive.
items.exampleCN: 历史是根据留存下来的文献写成的。

items.meaning: a person who studies or writes history
items.example: The historian compared tax rolls across three centuries.
items.exampleCN: 这位历史学家比较了三个世纪的税册。

items.meaning: the writing of history and its methods
items.example: Historiography examines how records were selected.
items.exampleCN: 史学史考察记录是如何被筛选的。

items.example: The story grew with each retelling.
items.exampleCN: 这个故事每讲一次就长大一些。

items.meaningCN: 戏剧化的、夸张的（词源无关，作对照）
items.example: His histrionic gestures amused the audience.
items.exampleCN: 他夸张的动作逗乐了观众。

latinEntries.meaning: a witness who knows the facts

definition_zh: 拘谨；抑制；克制；抑制作用；抑制因素
definition_en: a force that holds something back, whether an inner reluctance in a person or a process that slows or blocks a reaction, signal or growth
core_image: 一只手伸向门把，却在半空停住，手腕上像被一根看不见的带子拉住
scene: 第一次登台的学生站在幕布后，手心里全是汗，几次想开口都没出声。 Stage fright produced a strong inhibition in the young singer.
sceneCN: 这里指人在众人面前放不开的心理拘束（第 1 个义项：心理上的拘谨）；句意为怯场让这位年轻歌手产生了强烈的抑制。图中可辨识物件：幕布、发抖的手、停在半空的麦克风。

pos.zh: 拘谨；抑制；克制；抑制作用

derivatives.zh: 同一词根构成的动词，义为「抑制；阻止；使拘束」
由动词加过去分词词尾构成，义为「拘谨的；受压抑的」
由动词加表示「起……作用的」形容词尾构成，义为「抑制性的」
由动词加表示施动者或物质的名词尾构成，义为「抑制剂」
由否定前缀加过去分词构成，义为「无拘无束的」

senses.title: Inner shyness in company
senses.definition: a strong inner reluctance that makes a person hold back in social situations
senses.definitionCN: 在社交场合中使人退缩的强烈内在阻力
senses.example: Stage fright produced a strong inhibition in the young singer.
senses.exampleCN: 怯场让这位年轻歌手产生了强烈的抑制。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to hold in; psychology uses it for a brake applied from inside the person.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「扣住、收住」；心理学用它指人从内部踩下的刹车。

senses.title: Holding back an impulse
senses.definition: the checking of a desire, impulse or emotion before it becomes action
senses.definitionCN: 在欲望、冲动或情绪变成行动之前将其收住
senses.example: Years of strict training left him with an inhibition about asking for help.
senses.exampleCN: 多年严格训练让他对开口求助有一种克制。
senses.why: What is held in here is not a signal but a wish, and the holding is learned rather than mechanical.
senses.whyCN: 这里被收住的不是信号而是愿望，而且这种收住是学来的，不是机械的。

senses.title: Blocking a chemical reaction
senses.definition: the slowing or blocking of a chemical reaction, often by a substance that acts on an enzyme
senses.definitionCN: 对化学反应减速或阻断，常由作用于酶的物质造成
senses.example: Adding the compound caused inhibition of the enzyme within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 加入该化合物后，酶在几分钟内受到抑制。
senses.why: Biochemistry kept the image of a hand held back and applied it to molecules that stop a catalyst.
senses.whyCN: 生物化学保留「被拉住的手」这一意象，把它用在对催化剂下手的大分子上。

senses.title: Slowing of growth or division
senses.definition: a reduction in the growth, division or reproduction of cells or organisms
senses.definitionCN: 细胞或生物体在生长、分裂或繁殖上的减弱
senses.example: The extract showed clear inhibition of bacterial growth in the dish.
senses.exampleCN: 该提取物在培养皿中明显抑制了细菌生长。
senses.why: Here the thing held back is a whole population of cells, not one reaction step.
senses.whyCN: 这里被拦住的是整个细胞群体，而不是某一个反应步骤。

senses.title: Quieting of a nerve signal
senses.definition: the dampening of neural activity so that a signal becomes weaker or stops
senses.definitionCN: 神经活动被压弱，使信号变弱或停止
senses.example: The drug produces inhibition of pain signals in the spinal cord.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药物在脊髓中对疼痛信号产生抑制。
senses.why: The nervous system needs brakes as much as accelerators, and the word names those brakes.
senses.whyCN: 神经系统既需要加速器也需要刹车，这个词就指那些刹车。

senses.title: Suppression of a bodily function
senses.definition: the reduction or stopping of a secretion, reflex or organ function
senses.definitionCN: 对分泌、反射或器官功能的减弱或中止
senses.example: The treatment led to inhibition of acid secretion in the stomach.
senses.exampleCN: 该治疗导致胃酸分泌受到抑制。
senses.why: Medicine applies the same noun to any function that is made to quiet down.
senses.whyCN: 医学把同一个名词用于任何被压下去的功能。

senses.title: A social taboo or constraint
senses.definition: a rule or custom that keeps people from saying or doing something
senses.definitionCN: 使人不敢说或不敢做的规则与习俗
senses.example: The old inhibition against discussing money has weakened among younger buyers.
senses.exampleCN: 年轻消费者中，不谈钱的老禁忌已经减弱。
senses.why: The brake is no longer inside one mind but shared by a community.
senses.whyCN: 这时刹车不在某个人心里，而为一个群体所共有。

senses.title: Stiffness in performance
senses.definition: a lack of ease that makes a performance look guarded or forced
senses.definitionCN: 使表演显得拘束或做作的不自然状态
senses.example: The director asked the actors to drop their inhibition and move more freely.
senses.exampleCN: 导演要求演员放下拘束，动作更自由些。
senses.why: On stage the inner brake becomes visible: the body moves as if a strap were still on it.
senses.whyCN: 在舞台上，内心的刹车变得可见：身体动起来像还拴着带子。

intro.en: Inhibition comes from a Latin verb meaning to hold in, built from a prefix of inwardness and a root meaning to have or hold; psychology and biochemistry later gave it two technical lives.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语表示「扣在里面」的动词，由表示「向内」的前缀与表示「持有、握住」的词根构成；心理学与生物化学后来给了它两条技术生命。

items.en: habere meant to have, to hold, to keep in one's hand.
items.cn: habere 意为「有、握住、拿在手里」。

items.en: in- carried the sense of in or against, so inhibere was to hold in, check or restrain.
items.cn: in- 带有「在内、对着」的意思，因此 inhibere 意为「扣住、制止、约束」。

items.en: The past participle named something already held back, and it became the stem of the English family.
items.cn: 过去分词指已被收住的东西，后来成为英语这一族词的词干。

items.en: The action noun inhibitio named the act of holding in or checking.
items.cn: 动作名词 inhibitio 命名「收住、制止」这一行为。

items.en: English first used the word for restraining a legal or physical action; the exact first date is not certain, but the Latin line is clear.
items.cn: 英语最初用它指对法律行为或身体动作的制止；具体首见年份不确定，但拉丁来源线索清楚。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word split into an inner brake of the mind and a chemical brake on enzymes and growth.
items.cn: 二十世纪这个词分成两支：心智内部的刹车，以及作用于酶与生长的化学刹车。

note.en: The first group shares root or shape with inhibition; the second group names nearby brakes, and the note keeps their mechanisms apart.
note.cn: 第一组在词根或形音上与 inhibition 相近；第二组是邻近的「刹车」类词，说明中把它们的机制分开。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to hold back, slow or forbid a process or behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「抑制、阻碍、使拘束」。

entries.definition: Describing a person who is held back and shows it in behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 形容一个人受拘束，并在行为上表现出来。

entries.definition: A technical adjective for a signal, drug or cell that suppresses activity.
entries.definitionCN: 技术形容词，指压抑活动的信号、药物或细胞。

entries.definition: A substance or agent that slows a reaction or a biological process.
entries.definitionCN: 指减缓反应或生物过程的物质或因子。

entries.definition: A public display; it uses the same holding root with ex-, to hold out, so the direction is opposite.
entries.definitionCN: 指公开展览；同一「握住」词根配上表示「向外」的前缀，方向正好相反。

entries.definition: The act of living in a place; it looks close but comes from a verb for dwelling, not for holding in.
entries.definitionCN: 指居住在某地；形近，但来自表示「居住」的动词，而非「扣住」。

entries.definition: Self-control or an external limit that keeps action in check; broader and often deliberate.
entries.definitionCN: 指自我控制或外部限制，使行动受约束；更宽泛，且常是主动的。

entries.definition: Forceful putting down of a feeling, fact or activity; it stresses power and often concealment.
entries.definitionCN: 指对情绪、事实或活动的强力压下；强调权力，常含隐瞒。

entries.definition: An outside signal or action that disrupts a process rather than holding it from within.
entries.definitionCN: 指从外部扰乱过程的信号或行为，而非从内部拉住它。

entries.definition: A thing standing in the way that must be removed or gone round; it blocks movement, not a function.
entries.definitionCN: 指挡在路上、需要清除或绕开的东西；它阻碍的是移动，不是功能。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin hold-in image, the real psychology and biochemistry pairs, and the real sister words.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「扣住」意象、真实的心理学与生物化学搭配，以及真实的同族词。

normal.en: in- plus habere, to hold: inhibition is something held in, and the hand stops halfway.
normal.cn: in- 加 habere「握住」：抑制就是被扣在里面的东西，手停在半途。

normal.en: A car needs both an engine and a brake; a mind and a cell need inhibition too.
normal.cn: 汽车既需要引擎也需要刹车；心智与细胞同样需要抑制。

normal.en: Social inhibition, enzyme inhibition and growth inhibition are three real phrases.
normal.cn: 社交拘谨、酶抑制与生长抑制是三个真实搭配。

normal.en: Remove the brake and you get the negative adjective: uninhibited, without restraint.
normal.cn: 把刹车拆掉就得到否定形容词 uninhibited，即无拘无束。

normal.en: The same noun covers a shy singer and a stopped enzyme because both are held back.
normal.cn: 同一个名词既指害羞的歌手又指被抑制的酶，因为两者都是被拉住的。

abstract.en: A brake is not a flaw in the machine; without it, every impulse becomes movement.
abstract.cn: 刹车不是机器的缺陷；没有它，每个冲动都会变成动作。

abstract.en: Inhibition is pressure applied at a distance, felt as a hand that never quite arrives.
abstract.cn: 抑制是隔着距离施加的压力，感觉像一只始终到不了的手。

abstract.en: The word hides its own paradox: what holds you back also makes steady action possible.
abstract.cn: 这个词藏着悖论：拉住你的东西，也让稳定的行动成为可能。

examples.en: Her inhibition faded once the audience began to laugh with her.
examples.cn: 观众和她一起笑起来之后，她的拘束就消散了。

examples.en: The assay measures inhibition of the enzyme at several concentrations.
examples.cn: 该检测在多个浓度下测量酶的抑制程度。

examples.en: Cultural inhibition around silence made the meeting unusually slow.
examples.cn: 围绕沉默的文化禁忌让会议异常拖沓。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「因希比申」——把手往回收，就是抑制

root: 来自拉丁语 inhibere「扣住、制止」← in-「在内、对着」+ habere「握住、持有」，过去分词 inhibitus，动作名词 inhibitio；经法语进入英语。来源链清楚，首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from social shyness and held-back impulses to chemical, cellular, neural and medical brakes, then to taboo and stage stiffness.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从社交拘谨与收住的冲动，走到化学、细胞、神经与医学上的刹车，再到禁忌与舞台上的拘束。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaches for a door and stops in mid-air, held by an unseen strap.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手伸向门把，却在半空停住，被一根看不见的带子拉住。

branches.en: THE MIND'S BRAKE: shyness in company and a wish checked before it acts.
branches.cn: 心智的刹车：人前的拘谨，以及行动前被收住的愿望。

branches.en: THE CHEMISTRY AND THE CLINIC: reactions and secretions slowed by a substance.
branches.cn: 化学与临床：反应与分泌被某种物质减慢。

branches.en: THE CELL AND THE NERVE: growth and pain signals quieted from inside the body.
branches.cn: 细胞与神经：生长与疼痛信号在体内被压下去。

branches.en: THE SHARED TABOO: a rule that keeps a whole community from speaking.
branches.cn: 共享的禁忌：让整个群体缄口的一条规则。

branches.en: THE STRAP ON STAGE: a body that moves as if still held.
branches.cn: 舞台上的带子：身体动起来像仍被拉住。

intro.en: Inhibition is a Latin verb with an inward prefix, a holding root and an action-noun ending.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个拉丁动词加上内向前缀、握住词根与动作名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies habere, inhibere and inhibitio; the English family keeps the same holding image in every member.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 habere、inhibere 与 inhibitio；英语这一族的每个成员都保留同一个「握住」意象。

items.example: It turns holding into holding in.
The root is the hand that keeps the object.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根就是握着对象的那只手。

items.example: Prefix and root form the key verb.
items.exampleCN: 前缀与词根合成关键动词。

items.example: The participle supplies the adjective stem.
items.exampleCN: 分词提供了形容词词干。

items.example: It forms the action noun.
The base English verb keeps the brake.
items.exampleCN: 英语基础动词保留了刹车。

items.example: It forms inhibited, held back in behaviour.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 inhibited，指行为上受拘束。

items.example: It forms inhibitory, the technical adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它构成技术形容词 inhibitory。

items.example: It forms inhibitor, the substance that brakes.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 inhibitor，指踩刹车的物质。

items.example: It forms uninhibited, the brake released.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 uninhibited，即刹车被放开。

由过去分词构成，义为「拘谨的」
由「起……作用」词尾构成，义为「抑制性的」
由施动者词尾构成，义为「抑制剂」
由否定前缀构成，义为「无拘无束的」

definition_zh: 廉价饰品；小玩意儿；华而不实之物
definition_en: a small cheap showy ornament or trinket of little value
core_image: 圣诞树上挂着的闪闪发光却不值钱的彩球
scene: 集市摊上，孩子攥着一枚会转的亮片玩具不肯撒手。 She bought a shiny bauble at the fair.
sceneCN: 这里 bauble 指「廉价小玩意」（第 1 个义项：花哨不值钱的小饰品）；句意：她在集市买了个亮闪闪的小玩意。

pos.zh: 廉价饰品；小玩意

derivatives.zh: 挂满小饰物的（bauble + -ed）
古体 bauble 的旧式变体，义为「小玩物」——由同一词的旧拼写形式而来

senses.title: A cheap showy trinket
senses.definition: a small ornament of little worth
senses.definitionCN: 价值不高的装饰小件
senses.example: The stall sold glass baubles and beads.
senses.exampleCN: 摊位上卖玻璃彩球和珠子。
senses.why: Old French baubel named a child's toy; the toy grew pretty and stayed cheap.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 baubel 指儿童玩具；玩具变得花哨，依然廉价。

senses.title: The jester's stick
senses.definition: the baton with a head carried by a court fool
senses.definitionCN: 宫廷小丑手持的带头短杖
senses.example: The jester rapped the king's cup with his bauble.
senses.exampleCN: 小丑用短杖敲了敲国王的酒杯。
senses.why: The toy of children became the toy of fools.
senses.whyCN: 孩童的玩具成了弄臣的玩具。

senses.title: A thing of mock value
senses.definition: something valued beyond its worth, especially power or wealth
senses.definitionCN: 被高估之物，尤指权力或财富
senses.example: He called the crown a bauble and tossed it aside.
senses.exampleCN: 他称王冠为玩物，弃之一旁。
senses.why: Cromwell's phrase made the word a political sneer.
senses.whyCN: 克伦威尔之名言使该词成为政治讥语。

senses.title: Christmas-tree ornaments
senses.definition: decorative balls hung on a Christmas tree
senses.definitionCN: 挂在圣诞树上的装饰球
senses.example: They unpacked the baubles each December.
senses.exampleCN: 每年十二月他们取出圣诞彩球。
senses.why: The trinket found its yearly festival.
senses.whyCN: 小饰物找到自己一年一度的节日。

senses.title: Trivialities of fashion
senses.definition: showy but trivial accessories
senses.definitionCN: 花哨却琐碎的服饰配件
senses.example: Her desk is crowded with pink baubles.
senses.exampleCN: 她的书桌上摆满粉色小饰物。
senses.why: Cheap ornament colonizes any surface.
senses.whyCN: 廉价饰品能占领任何台面。

senses.title: Literary contempt
senses.definition: a writer's term for worthless honors or trifles
senses.definitionCN: 作家指称无价值荣衔或琐物的用语
senses.example: Poets have mocked the baubles of the court for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 数百年来诗人讥讽宫廷的虚饰。
senses.why: The sneer is older than the festival.
senses.whyCN: 讥讽早于节日。

senses.title: A child's toy
senses.definition: the original sense, a plaything
senses.definitionCN: 本义：玩具
senses.example: Old books list baubles among children's plays.
senses.exampleCN: 旧书将玩具列入儿童游艺。
senses.why: The French root said it first.
senses.whyCN: 法语词根最初说的正是它。

senses.title: Baubled display
senses.definition: decked with trinkets
senses.definitionCN: 缀满小饰物的
senses.example: a baubled headdress for the dance
senses.exampleCN: 舞会用的缀饰头冠
senses.why: The noun turns descriptive.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为描写。

intro.en: Bauble comes from Old French baubel, a child's plaything, perhaps a reduplicated form of a childish sound; English took it in the fourteenth century.
intro.cn: bauble 出自古法语 baubel「儿童玩具」，或为孩童口语的叠音造词；英语于十四世纪借入。

items.en: Reduplicated syllables make many toy words.
items.cn: 叠音音节造出许多玩具词。

items.en: baubel named a trinket or toy.
items.cn: 古法语 baubel 指小饰物或玩具。

items.en: English borrowed it as the jester's stick and the toy.
items.cn: 英语借入，兼指弄臣短杖与玩具。

items.en: The political sneer about crowns became famous.
items.cn: 关于王冠的政治讥语变得有名。

items.en: The Christmas ornament sense now leads seasonal usage.

normalIntro.cn: bauble 闪亮如泡泡，内里却无价值：珠宝中的泡泡。

definition_zh: 理论框架；指导研究并解释现象的一整套理论、假设与概念结构
definition_en: an organized set of theories, assumptions and concepts that guides a study and explains what it observes
core_image: 一张摊开的大图纸上，几根主梁先立稳，再把各块薄板搭到梁上，整间屋子的受力关系一眼可见
scene: 开题报告写到研究思路一节，导师要求学生先把所依据的理论体系搭清楚，再谈具体方法。 Every thesis needs a theoretical framework before the methods are chosen.
sceneCN: 这里指研究开始前先搭好的理论体系（第 1 个义项：指导研究的理论结构）；句意为每篇论文在选定方法之前都需要一个理论框架。

pos.zh: 理论框架；理论体系

collocations.zh: 以某一理论框架为基础

derivatives.zh: 由希腊语「观看、沉思」而来的名词，义为「理论；学说」
由「理论」加表示「属于……的」形容词尾构成，义为「理论的」
在形容词后加副词尾，义为「在理论上」
加表示「从事者」的名词尾，义为「理论家」
加表示「使……化」的动词尾，义为「建立理论」

senses.title: The overall theory that guides a study
senses.titleCN: 统领整项研究的理论结构
senses.definition: the organized body of theory that defines what a study looks at and how it interprets results
senses.definitionCN: 界定研究看什么、如何解释结果的成体系理论
senses.example: The theoretical framework draws on two models of learning.
senses.exampleCN: 这个理论框架借用了两种学习模型。
senses.why: A framework is a load-bearing structure, and theory supplies the beams that hold a study upright.
senses.whyCN: 框架是承重结构，而理论提供把研究撑起来的梁。

senses.title: A set of assumptions and definitions
senses.definition: the assumptions and defined terms that a study accepts before any data are collected
senses.definitionCN: 研究在收集数据之前就已接受的一组假设与界定好的术语
senses.example: Her theoretical framework treats motivation as a stable trait.
senses.exampleCN: 她的理论框架把动机视为一种稳定特质。
senses.why: Every framework begins by fixing what its words mean, just as a building begins with fixed dimensions.
senses.whyCN: 每个框架都先固定词的含义，正如建筑先固定尺寸。

senses.title: An explanatory scheme from a discipline
senses.titleCN: 来自某一学科的解释方案
senses.definition: a recognized explanatory scheme borrowed from a field such as psychology, economics or sociology
senses.definitionCN: 从心理学、经济学或社会学等领域借来的、被认可的解释方案
senses.example: The study used a sociological theoretical framework to explain voting.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究用社会学的理论框架解释投票行为。
senses.why: Disciplines keep ready-made schemes, and borrowing one gives a study an established language for its findings.
senses.whyCN: 学科各自备有成套方案，借来一套就让研究结果有了既成的解释语言。

senses.title: The theory chapter of a thesis
senses.titleCN: 学位论文中的理论章节
senses.definition: the section of a thesis that reviews and justifies the theory chosen for the project
senses.definitionCN: 学位论文中评述并论证所选理论的那一部分
senses.example: Chapter two sets out the theoretical framework in twenty pages.
senses.exampleCN: 第二章用二十页篇幅交代理论框架。
senses.why: In academic writing the abstract structure becomes a named section, so the phrase also labels a chapter.
senses.whyCN: 在学术写作里，抽象结构变成一个具名章节，因此这个词组也指一章。

senses.title: A lens for reading the data
senses.definition: the perspective through which observations are selected, sorted and given meaning
senses.definitionCN: 用来筛选、归类并赋予观察以意义的视角
senses.example: Through this theoretical framework, silence in the interviews counts as data.
senses.exampleCN: 透过这个理论框架，访谈中的沉默也算作数据。
senses.why: Theory decides what counts as relevant, which is like a lens that brings one part of the field into focus.
senses.whyCN: 理论决定什么算相关，就像镜片把视野中的一部分对焦。

senses.title: A source of testable hypotheses
senses.definition: the part of a theory that predicts relationships which the study can then test
senses.definitionCN: 理论中预测各种关系、可供研究随后检验的部分
senses.example: The theoretical framework predicts that feedback raises persistence.
senses.exampleCN: 这个理论框架预测反馈会提高坚持度。
senses.why: A theory earns its place in research by making predictions, so the framework is also a hypothesis machine.
senses.whyCN: 理论靠做出预测在研究里立足，因此框架也是一台生产假设的机器。

senses.title: The boundary of a study's claims
senses.definition: the limits that theory sets on what the study can reasonably claim
senses.definitionCN: 理论为本研究可以合理主张的范围划定的界限
senses.example: The theoretical framework limits the findings to adult learners.
senses.exampleCN: 这个理论框架把结论限定在成年学习者范围内。
senses.why: A frame holds a picture inside its edges, and theory marks how far a conclusion may travel.
senses.whyCN: 画框把画面圈在边内，理论则标出结论能走多远。

senses.title: The standard for judging fit
senses.definition: the benchmark used to decide whether findings are consistent with the theory
senses.definitionCN: 用来判断研究结果是否与理论相符的基准
senses.example: Reviewers asked whether the results fit the theoretical framework.
senses.exampleCN: 审稿人追问结果是否与理论框架相符。
senses.why: Once a scheme is adopted, it becomes a yardstick, and mismatches between results and theory become visible.
senses.whyCN: 方案一旦被采用就成为尺子，结果与理论不合之处便显现出来。

intro.en: Theoretical framework pairs a Greek word for contemplative viewing with an English word for a load-bearing structure. Theory supplies the beams; framework supplies the shape that holds them together.
intro.cn: 这个词组把希腊语中表示「沉思观看」的词，与英语中表示承重结构的词配在一起。理论提供梁，框架提供把它们拢住的形状。

items.en: Theoria meant a viewing or contemplation, especially the official viewing of a sacred rite; its deeper link to a word for sight is plausible but not certain.
items.cn: 这个词指观看或沉思，尤指对宗教仪式的正式观礼；它与表示「看」的词有联系，但这一点只是推测，并非确证。

items.en: Late Latin took the Greek adjective for «belonging to viewing» and passed it to European languages as the word for theory.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语取来这个希腊形容词，义为「与观看有关的」，再传给欧洲各语言，成为「理论」一词。

items.en: English theory appeared in the sixteenth century for a speculative scheme of knowledge, as opposed to practice.
items.cn: 英语的「理论」在十六世纪出现，指与实践相对的思辨知识体系。

items.en: Framian meant to be useful or to advance, and the related noun frame named something that gives shape and support.
items.cn: 这个古英语动词意为「有用、推进」，相关名词指给出形状与支撑的东西。

items.en: Frame and work joined in the sixteenth or seventeenth century for a supporting structure; the earliest record is uncertain.
items.cn: 「框」与「工」在十六或十七世纪合成，指起支撑作用的结构；最早记录年代不确定。

items.en: Social science fixed the two words together in the twentieth century for the theory structure that a study rests on.
items.cn: 社会科学在二十世纪把这两个词固定组合，指一项研究所依托的理论结构。

note.en: The first group belongs to the theory family or merely looks similar; the second group names other kinds of research structure.
note.cn: 第一组属于「理论」同族或只是形近；第二组指其他类型的研究结构。

entries.definition: An organized set of ideas meant to explain a class of facts.
entries.definitionCN: 指用来解释一类事实的成体系观点。

entries.definition: Concerned with theory rather than practice or measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 指关涉理论而非实践或测量的。

entries.definition: A person who builds or studies theories.
entries.definitionCN: 指建构或研究理论的人。

entries.definition: A statement proved from accepted premises; it shares the viewing root.
entries.definitionCN: 指由公认前提证明的命题；与「观看」词根同源。

entries.definition: A supporting structure, whether physical or conceptual.
entries.definitionCN: 指起支撑作用的结构，可以是实物也可以是概念。

entries.definition: The study of religion; it begins with the word for god, not for viewing.
entries.definitionCN: 指宗教学；起首是「神」的词，而非「观看」。

entries.definition: A researcher's own map of concepts and their links, rather than a borrowed theory.
entries.definitionCN: 指研究者自己绘制的概念及关系图，而非借来的理论。

entries.definition: The structure that organizes how a analysis will break a problem into parts.
entries.definitionCN: 指把问题拆成部分来分析时所依的结构。

entries.definition: A simplified representation of the variables and paths a study will examine.
entries.definitionCN: 指对研究要考察的变量与路径的简化表示。

entries.definition: A whole way of thinking shared by a field, larger than one study's framework.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个领域共有的整套思维方式，比单项研究的框架更大。

entries.definition: A specific testable prediction, narrower than a framework.
entries.definitionCN: 指具体可检验的预测，比框架窄。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the load-bearing picture and the real academic phrases around theory.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用承重结构的画面，以及围绕「理论」的真实学术搭配。

normal.en: Theory is the beam and framework is the shape: neither stands without the other.
normal.cn: 理论是梁，框架是形，两者缺一都立不住。

normal.en: A framework carries weight, so a weak theory shows up as a study that sags under its own claims.
normal.cn: 框架要承重，理论一弱，研究就会在自己的结论下塌下去。

normal.en: The phrase is standard in proposals, where it names the chapter that justifies the theory.
normal.cn: 这个词组在开题报告里是标准说法，用来指论证理论的那一章。

normal.en: A theoretical framework predicts; a conceptual framework organizes. The pair is often confused.
normal.cn: 理论框架负责预测，概念框架负责组织，两者常被混用。

normal.en: The frame around a picture decides what is inside the picture.
normal.cn: 画框决定什么在画面之内。

abstract.en: A framework is visible only when something pushes against it; theory is tested by findings that do not fit.
abstract.cn: 框架只有在被推挤时才显形，理论则靠不吻合的结果来检验。

abstract.en: Every study stands inside a frame it did not build, and the frame quietly decides what counts as evidence.
abstract.cn: 每项研究都站在一个自己没搭的框架里，这个框架悄悄决定什么算证据。

abstract.en: Beams are chosen before the room is used, which is why the theory must come before the method.
abstract.cn: 梁在使用房间之前就选好，所以理论必须先于方法。

examples.en: The paper builds its theoretical framework on two competing models of memory.
examples.cn: 这篇论文把理论框架建立在两种相互竞争的记忆模型上。

examples.en: Without a theoretical framework, the interviews produced anecdotes rather than findings.
examples.cn: 没有理论框架，这些访谈只产出轶事而不是研究发现。

examples.en: The committee asked the student to align the method with the theoretical framework.
examples.cn: 委员会要求学生让方法与理论框架保持一致。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「理论」是梁，「框架」是框：先立梁再围框，一套撑起研究的骨架就是理论框架

root: 「理论」源自希腊语 theoria「观看、沉思」，经晚期拉丁语 theoreticus 进入欧洲语言。「框架」由古英语 framian「有用、推进」与 work「工、作」合成，十六七世纪起指承重结构；两个词在二十世纪社会科学中被固定组合。最早记录年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the whole structure to its edges: the guiding theory, the assumptions, a borrowed scheme, a thesis chapter, a lens on data, a source of hypotheses, the limit of claims, and the standard of fit.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从整体走向边缘：统领理论、假设与定义、借来的解释方案、论文理论章、解读数据的镜片、假设的来源、结论的边界、契合的标准。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a frame of beams is raised first, and every later panel is fixed to those beams.
core.cn: 核心意象：先立起一副梁架，此后每一块板都固定在这副梁上。

branches.en: THE GUIDING THEORY: the borrowed scheme that decides what the study examines.
branches.cn: 统领理论：决定研究考察什么的借用方案。

branches.en: THE FIXED ASSUMPTIONS: definitions and beliefs accepted before data arrive.
branches.cn: 既定假设：在数据到来前就接受的界定与信念。

branches.en: THE WRITTEN CHAPTER: the part of a thesis that justifies the choice.
branches.cn: 成文章节：论文中论证该选择的部分。

branches.en: THE WORKING LENS: the perspective that sorts data and predicts relations.
branches.cn: 工作镜片：筛选数据并预测关系的视角。

branches.en: THE EDGE OF THE FRAME: what the study may claim and how fit is judged.
branches.cn: 框的边缘：研究可以主张什么，以及如何判断契合。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Greek-derived theory word to an Old English structure word, and both halves still carry their original pictures.
intro.cn: 这个词组把希腊来源的理论词与古英语的结构词接在一起，两半至今都带着各自的原始画面。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies theoreticus; the structure half is native English and has no Latin entry.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「理论的」这一形容词；结构那一半是英语本族词，没有拉丁语条目。

items.example: It marks the neighbouring phrase conceptual framework.
items.exampleCN: 它标出邻近的「概念框架」一词。

senses.definition: a unit that tells how loud a sound is

senses.why: A bar of volume steps climbing one by one.

definition_zh: 与……共同；连同……一起（多用于正式、法律与技术文本）
definition_en: together with another person, body or measure; used in formal, legal and technical writing
core_image: 两名工程师在同一台设备前同时插入两张授权卡
scene: 两名工程师在同一台设备前同时插入两张授权卡。 The test was run in conjunction with the manufacturer.
sceneCN: 这里取「与……共同」（第 1 个义项：两方合作完成一件事）；句意为这项测试是与制造商共同进行的。

pos.zh: 介词短语：与……共同；连同……一起（正式）

derivatives.zh: 连词；结合
使结合
连接的；结合的
交叉点；接合处
共同地

senses.title: Working together with another party
senses.definition: used to say that two parties carry out one task together
senses.definitionCN: 表示两方共同完成同一项任务
senses.example: The test was run in conjunction with the manufacturer.
senses.exampleCN: 这项测试是与制造商共同进行的。
senses.why: The phrase names a partner rather than a tool, so the two sides share responsibility for the same act.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语点出的是伙伴而非工具，因此两方对同一动作共同负责。

senses.title: Combining two measures at once
senses.definition: used to say that one measure is applied together with another
senses.definitionCN: 表示一项措施与另一项措施同时施用
senses.example: The drug was given in conjunction with rest and diet.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药连同休息与饮食调整一并施用。
senses.why: Here the second item is not an agent but an accompanying measure, which shifts the phrase from partnership to combination.
senses.whyCN: 此处第二项不是行动者，而是伴随措施，短语于是从「合作」转向「组合」。

senses.title: Technical pairing of devices or systems
senses.definition: used in manuals to say that one device or system must be used together with another
senses.definitionCN: 在手册中说明某设备或系统须与另一设备配合使用
senses.example: The sensor works in conjunction with the control unit.
senses.exampleCN: 这个传感器与控制单元配合工作。
senses.why: Technical writing uses the phrase to describe a required pairing rather than a temporary collaboration.
senses.whyCN: 技术写作借此描述必需的配对，而非临时的协作。

senses.title: Joint handling under a contract
senses.titleCN: 法律合同：连同……一并处理
senses.definition: in legal drafting, used to say that a matter is handled together with another provision or party
senses.definitionCN: 在法律起草中，表示某事项与另一条款或另一方一并处理
senses.example: The claim was settled in conjunction with the earlier agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 这项索赔是连同早先的协议一并解决的。
senses.why: Contracts use the phrase to bind two instruments into one settlement without merging them into a single clause.
senses.whyCN: 合同借此把两份文书绑进同一处理，却不合并成一条。

senses.title: Official joint action
senses.definition: used in official statements to name an authority acting together with another body
senses.definitionCN: 在官方声明中点出某机构与另一机构共同行动
senses.example: The inquiry was opened in conjunction with local authorities.
senses.exampleCN: 调查是会同地方当局启动的。
senses.why: Institutional prose needs to show shared authority without saying who leads, and the phrase keeps the balance.
senses.whyCN: 机构文字需要显示共同授权、又不说明谁主导，这个短语保持平衡。

senses.title: Combined treatment in medicine
senses.titleCN: 医学：联合用药、联合治疗
senses.definition: used in clinical writing to describe one treatment given together with another
senses.definitionCN: 在临床写作中，描述一种治疗与另一种同时使用
senses.example: The therapy is most effective in conjunction with physical exercise.
senses.exampleCN: 这种疗法与体育锻炼联合使用效果最好。
senses.why: Clinical writing distinguishes a single agent from a regimen, and the phrase marks the regimen.
senses.whyCN: 临床写作要区分单一药物与联合方案，这个短语标出后者。

senses.title: The formal stand-in for a plain phrase
senses.titleCN: 句末后置：正式替代「与……一起」
senses.definition: placed after the verb as a formal alternative to the plainer together with
senses.definitionCN: 放在动词之后，作为更正式的说法替代日常的「与……一起」
senses.example: The two departments submitted the report in conjunction with each other.
senses.exampleCN: 两个部门共同提交了这份报告。
senses.why: Trailing position keeps the main verb in focus while raising the register of the whole sentence.
senses.whyCN: 后置让主要动词保持焦点，同时抬高整句语域。

senses.title: Joint sponsorship of an event
senses.titleCN: 事件语境：联合主办、共同发布
senses.definition: used to name a second organization that shares the staging or issuing of something
senses.definitionCN: 点出共同承办或共同发布的第二个组织
senses.example: The exhibition was opened in conjunction with the city museum.
senses.exampleCN: 展览是与市博物馆联合举办的。
senses.why: Events and publications use the phrase to share credit between institutions without naming a hierarchy.
senses.whyCN: 活动与出版物借此在机构间分摊功劳，而不排出高低。

intro.en: Conjunction comes from Latin coniunctio, from coniungere, to join together, itself con-, with, and iungere, to join, from the yoke root iug-. The Latin line is clear.
intro.cn: conjunction 来自拉丁语 coniunctio，词根 coniungere 意为「连在一起」，由 con-「共同」与 iungere「连接」构成，后者出自「轭」的词根 iug-。拉丁语线索清楚。

items.en: Iugum, yoke, is the image behind the whole family: two things bound under one beam.
items.cn: iugum 意为「轭」，是整族词的画面：两物被同一根横梁套住。

items.en: Iungere meant to join or unite, and supplied the verb behind conjunction.
items.cn: iungere 意为连接、结合，提供了 conjunction 背后的动词。

items.en: The noun named a joining together, in grammar as well as in general use.
items.cn: 这个名词指连在一起，既用于语法，也用于一般意义。

items.en: English conjunction appears in the Middle English period; the date is approximate.
items.cn: 英语 conjunction 见于中古英语，年代为约数。

items.en: The phrase with this preposition settles in modern legal, technical and official writing.
items.cn: 带这个介词的短语在近代法律、技术与官方文字中定型。

note.en: The first group shares the together-slot but stresses connection, compliance or plain accompaniment; the second group holds adverbs and phrases of shared action.
note.cn: 第一组同样表示「一起」，但侧重连接、遵守或单纯伴随；第二组是共同行动的副词与短语。

entries.definition: It usually means concerning a matter, not acting together on it.
entries.definitionCN: 它通常指「关于某事项」，而非共同去做。

entries.definition: It names a rule being followed and never a partner.
entries.definitionCN: 它点出所遵循的规则，从不点出伙伴。

entries.definition: It is the everyday phrase for accompanying items and carries no institutional weight.
entries.definitionCN: 它是最平常的伴随说法，没有机构分量。

entries.definition: It adds a companion item in neutral prose.
entries.definitionCN: 在中性文字中追加伴随项。

entries.definition: It states that two parties share an act, usually without naming them.
entries.definitionCN: 说明两方共担一事，通常不点名。

entries.definition: It stresses a business relationship rather than a single shared task.
entries.definitionCN: 强调商业关系，而非单次共同任务。

entries.definition: It describes two measures merged into one effect.
entries.definitionCN: 描述两项措施合并为一个效果。

entries.definition: It stresses timing and organization rather than shared credit.
entries.definitionCN: 强调时机与组织协调，而非共同署名。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real yoke root, the real partners and the real register.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用真实「轭」词根、真实伙伴与真实语域。

normal.en: A yoke binds two animals under one beam, and the word keeps that picture of joint work.
normal.cn: 轭把两头牲口套在同一横梁下，这个词保留了共同劳作的画面。

normal.en: It is formal: contracts, manuals and official notices use it, not lunchtime chat.
normal.cn: 它很正式：合同、手册与官方通告用它，午饭闲谈不用。

normal.en: The partner may be a company, an agency, a treatment or a measure.
normal.cn: 伙伴可以是公司、机构、疗法或措施。

normal.en: It differs from compliance: a rule is followed, a partner acts alongside.
normal.cn: 它与「遵守」不同：规则被遵循，伙伴则并肩行动。

normal.en: At the end of a clause it raises the tone of the whole sentence.
normal.cn: 放在从句末尾，它会抬高整句语气。

abstract.en: Like two keys turned in two locks at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 像两把钥匙在同一刻转动两把锁。

abstract.en: Like two beams tied under one yoke so they pull together.
abstract.cn: 像两根梁被同一副轭套住，一起发力。

abstract.en: Like two signatures on one page, neither above the other.
abstract.cn: 像同一页上的两个签名，谁也不比谁高。

examples.en: The survey was designed in conjunction with two local hospitals.
examples.cn: 这项调查是与两家地方医院共同设计的。

examples.en: The software must be installed in conjunction with the driver.
examples.cn: 这个软件必须与驱动程序配合安装。

examples.en: The campaign was launched in conjunction with the health ministry.
examples.cn: 这场活动是与卫生部联合发起的。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses split by the second term: a partner, an accompanying measure, a paired device, a contract instrument, an official body, a treatment, a trailing formal phrase, and a co-sponsor.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项按第二项的性质区分：伙伴、伴随措施、配对设备、合同文书、官方机构、治疗方案、句末正式替代、共同主办方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two authorization cards inserted into one machine at the same moment.
core.cn: 核心意象：两张授权卡在同一刻插入同一台设备。

branches.en: THE PARTNER: a company, an authority or a co-sponsor acts alongside.
branches.cn: 伙伴：公司、机构或共同主办方并肩行动。

branches.en: THE REGIMEN: measures and treatments are applied together.
branches.cn: 方案：措施与疗法一并施用。

branches.en: THE PAIRING: a device requires another unit to work.
branches.cn: 配对：设备需要另一单元才能工作。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENT: two legal documents are settled as one matter.
branches.cn: 文书：两份法律文件作为一事处理。

branches.en: THE REGISTER: trailing position makes plain accompaniment formal.
branches.cn: 语域：后置把日常伴随抬成正式说法。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin noun of yoking with an English preposition; the yoke root is the core image.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁语「套轭」名词与英语介词结合；轭词根是核心画面。

latinIntro.en: The Latin etyma are iungere, to join, and iugum, yoke; coniunctio is the noun built on them.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词源是 iungere「连接」与 iugum「轭」；coniunctio 是在其上构成的名词。

definition_zh: 回报率；收益率
definition_en: the gain from an investment expressed as a percentage of its cost
core_image: 一只天平，一端放投入，另一端放回收，两个数字相除得出一个百分比
scene: 项目评审会上，分析师把预计收益与投入成本相除，得到一个按年计算的百分比。 Analysts calculated the rate of return before approving the project.
sceneCN: 这里指「回报率」，对应第 1 个义项：收益相对于投入的百分比；句意为分析师在批准项目之前先计算了回报率。画面要点：评审桌、计算器、成本与收益两栏。

pos.zh: 回报率；收益率（常与投资、项目或资产连用）

senses.title: Gain measured against cost
senses.titleCN: 收益相对于投入的比率
senses.definition: the profit or income from an investment stated as a percentage of the amount invested
senses.definitionCN: 投资所得利润或收入占投入金额的百分比
senses.example: The project offers a rate of return of nine percent.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目提供百分之九的回报率。
senses.why: Rate supplies the proportion and return supplies the gain, so the phrase puts one number over another to make them comparable.
senses.whyCN: rate 提供比例，return 提供增益，这个短语把一个数放在另一个数之上，使两者可比。

senses.title: The annualized rate
senses.definition: the rate of return recalculated as if it accrued over one year
senses.definitionCN: 按一年为期限重新折算的回报率
senses.example: The fund reports an annualized rate of return.
senses.exampleCN: 该基金报告的是年化回报率。
senses.why: Periods differ, so the percentage is stretched or compressed to a one-year standard before comparisons are made.
senses.whyCN: 各期长度不同，于是百分比先被拉伸或压缩到一年的标准，再作比较。

senses.title: The minimum acceptable rate
senses.titleCN: 要求达到的最低回报率
senses.definition: the lowest return an investor or firm will accept before committing funds
senses.definitionCN: 投资者或公司在投入资金前愿意接受的最低回报
senses.example: The board set a required rate of return for new plants.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会为新工厂设定了必要回报率。
senses.why: The measure becomes a gate: capital is not released unless the projected percentage clears the threshold.
senses.whyCN: 这个指标变成一道闸门：预期百分比不过门槛，资金就不放行。

senses.title: The internal rate of return
senses.definition: the discount rate at which a project's inflows and outflows have a net present value of zero
senses.definitionCN: 使项目现金流入与流出的净现值为零的折现率
senses.example: The internal rate of return was above the cost of capital.
senses.exampleCN: 内部收益率高于资本成本。
senses.why: Here the rate is solved from the cash flows themselves rather than stated in advance, so the project's own pattern sets the number.
senses.whyCN: 这里的比率由现金流本身解出，而不是事先给定，项目的自身模式决定了这个数字。

senses.title: The real rate after inflation
senses.titleCN: 扣除通胀后的实际回报率
senses.definition: the rate of return adjusted for inflation
senses.definitionCN: 经通胀调整后的回报率
senses.example: A nominal gain can be a negative real rate of return.
senses.exampleCN: 名义上的增益也可能是负的实际回报率。
senses.why: Money gains can shrink in purchasing power, so the measured percentage is corrected to show what it really buys.
senses.whyCN: 金钱上的增益可能被购买力侵蚀，因此测得的百分比要修正，以显示它真正能买到什么。

senses.title: The accounting rate of return
senses.definition: a rate calculated from accounting profit rather than cash flow
senses.definitionCN: 依据会计利润而非现金流计算的比率
senses.example: The accounting rate of return ignores the timing of cash.
senses.exampleCN: 会计收益率忽略现金的时间分布。
senses.why: Different records produce different numbers, so the phrase is qualified by the bookkeeping method that supplies the gain.
senses.whyCN: 不同的账目产生不同的数字，因此这个短语要用提供增益的记账方法来限定。

senses.title: The expected rate
senses.definition: the return an investor anticipates before the outcome is known
senses.definitionCN: 结果未知前投资者预期的回报
senses.example: Investors demand more for a risky expected rate of return.
senses.exampleCN: 投资者对高风险的预期回报要求更高。
senses.why: Before the fact the percentage is a forecast, so the phrase shifts from a realized gain to an anticipated one.
senses.whyCN: 在结果出来之前，百分比是预测，于是这个短语从已实现的增益转到预期的增益。

senses.title: The social rate of return
senses.definition: the return to society from public spending, including benefits not captured in cash
senses.definitionCN: 公共支出给社会带来的回报，包括未以现金体现的益处
senses.example: Vaccination programmes show a high social rate of return.
senses.exampleCN: 疫苗接种项目显示出很高的社会回报率。
senses.why: The gain is widened from private money to public benefit, so the same ratio is applied to health, education and infrastructure.
senses.whyCN: 增益从私人金钱扩大到公共益处，同一个比率于是被用到健康、教育与基础设施上。

intro.en: Rate of return joins rate, from a Latin word for a reckoned share, with return, from a French verb for turning back. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这一短语把「比率」与「回报」两个词组合起来：前者出自拉丁语表示计算出的份额，后者出自法语表示转回去的动词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Reri meant to reckon, think or judge, and it built words about calculation and reason.
items.cn: reri 意为计算、思考、判断，构成了一批表示计算与理性的词。

items.en: Rata pars meant a fixed or reckoned share, and the adjective rata became the English noun rate.
items.cn: rata pars 意为确定或计算出的份额，形容词 rata 后来成为英语名词 rate。

items.en: Rate entered English as a proportion, a standard or a charge fixed by calculation.
items.cn: rate 进入英语时指比例、标准或经计算确定的收费。

items.en: Return took on the sense of the gain that comes back from capital, supplying the second half of the phrase.
items.cn: return 获得「资本带回的增益」这一意义，提供短语的后半。

items.en: Engineers and investors began to compare projects by the percentage that came back each year, fixing rate of return as a technical phrase.
items.cn: 工程师与投资者开始用每年返回的百分比比较项目，回报率这一说法于是固定为专业短语。

items.en: Modern finance multiplied its variants: internal, real, required, expected, accounting and social.
items.cn: 现代金融衍生出许多变体：内部、实际、必要、预期、会计与社会。

note.en: The first group is built from the same reckoning root; the second group contains related measures that answer different questions.
note.cn: 第一组建立在同一个「计算」词根上；第二组是回答不同问题的相关指标。

entries.definition: A proportion or a charge per unit; alone it says nothing about gain, only about a measured relation.
entries.definitionCN: 比例或每单位的收费；单独使用时不表示增益，只表示被衡量的关系。

entries.definition: A relation between two quantities expressed as one divided by the other; a rate of return is one kind of ratio.
entries.definitionCN: 两个数量之间以一个除另一个的关系；回报率是比率的一种。

entries.definition: A fixed allowance of food or supplies; it is a reckoned share, not a financial gain.
entries.definitionCN: 食物或物资的定额；它是计算出的份额，不是金融增益。

entries.definition: Based on reason or calculation; it shares the reckoning root but describes thinking, not returns.
entries.definitionCN: 基于理性或计算的；共享「计算」词根，但描述思维而非回报。

entries.definition: The gain from an investment relative to its cost; it is the broader phrase, while rate of return often appears in project and portfolio arithmetic.
entries.definitionCN: 投资增益相对于成本；它是更宽的说法，而回报率常用于项目与组合计算。

entries.definition: Income from an investment as a percentage, usually ignoring price change; rate of return can include both income and capital gain.
entries.definitionCN: 投资收入以百分比计，通常忽略价格变动；回报率可同时包括收入与资本增值。

entries.definition: The percentage charged for a loan; it is the price of money, not the gain from using it.
entries.definitionCN: 贷款的收费百分比；它是资金的价格，而不是使用资金得到的增益。

entries.definition: The ability of a business to produce profit; it is a quality, while a rate of return is a number.
entries.definitionCN: 企业产生利润的能力；它是性质，而回报率是一个数字。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real reckoning root, the real turning root and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「计算」词根、真实的「转回」词根与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Rate means a reckoned proportion; return means gain coming back; together they put gain over cost.
normal.cn: rate 是算出的比例，return 是转回的增益；合起来就是把增益放在成本之上。

normal.en: The phrase answers one question: for every unit put in, how much comes back?
normal.cn: 这个短语回答一个问题：每投入一个单位，能回来多少？

normal.en: Annual, real, required, expected, internal and social are fixed qualifiers that change the question slightly.
normal.cn: 年度、实际、必要、预期、内部与社会这些固定限定语略微改变问题。

normal.en: Required rate is a gate; internal rate is solved from cash flows; real rate removes inflation.
normal.cn: 必要回报率是闸门；内部收益率由现金流解出；实际回报率扣除通胀。

normal.en: Rate of return is a ratio, so it is always a percentage or a decimal, never a sum of money.
normal.cn: 回报率是一个比率，所以总是百分比或小数，而不是一笔金额。

abstract.en: Picture a balance with cost on one pan and gain on the other, and a small percentage printed where the beam settles.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平，一端放成本，另一端放增益，横梁停住处印着一个小百分比。

abstract.en: Picture the same percentage stretched over twelve months, then squeezed back for a single quarter.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个百分比被拉到十二个月，再压回一个季度。

abstract.en: Picture a thermometer whose mercury is purchasing power, falling even while the money number rises.
abstract.cn: 想象一支温度计里的水银是购买力，金钱数字上升时它却在下降。

examples.en: The plant achieved a rate of return above the industry average.
examples.cn: 这家工厂的回报率高于行业平均。

examples.en: A negative real rate of return erodes savings silently.
examples.cn: 负的实际回报率在不知不觉中侵蚀储蓄。

examples.en: They rejected the plan because its internal rate of return was too low.
examples.cn: 他们否决了该计划，因为其内部收益率太低。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「回来的比例」——投入一笔钱，看返回来的部分占多少 → 回报率

root: rate 出自拉丁语 rata pars「计算出的份额」，源于 reri「计算、判断」；return 出自法语表示「转回去」的动词。两者合指收益相对于投入的比率。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all express one ratio, then qualify it by time, by threshold, by method, by inflation, by expectation and by who receives the benefit.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都表达同一个比率，再按时间、门槛、方法、通胀、预期与受益者加以限定。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance with cost on one pan and gain on the other, printing a percentage.
core.cn: 核心意象：一架天平，一端放成本，另一端放增益，并印出一个百分比。

branches.en: BASE RATIO: gain divided by cost gives the plain measure.
branches.cn: 基础比率：增益除以成本，得到最朴素的指标。

branches.en: TIME AND EXPECTATION: the same ratio is annualized, or projected before the outcome is known.
branches.cn: 时间与预期：同一比率被年化，或在结果未知前被预测。

branches.en: THRESHOLD: the ratio becomes a minimum that capital must clear.
branches.cn: 门槛：这个比率成为资金必须越过的下限。

branches.en: METHOD: cash flows solve an internal rate, while accounting profit produces a book rate.
branches.cn: 方法：现金流解出内部收益率，会计利润产生账面收益率。

branches.en: REAL AND SOCIAL: inflation is removed, or private gain is widened to public benefit.
branches.cn: 实际与社会：或扣除通胀，或把私人增益扩大到公共益处。

intro.en: Rate of return is a phrase made of two Latin-derived words, and each brings a family of related terms.
intro.cn: 这一短语由两个拉丁来源词构成，各自带来一族相关词。

latinIntro.en: Latin reri 'to reckon' gives rate, ratio, ration, rational and reason; return comes through French from a Latin turning word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 reri「计算」衍生 rate、ratio、ration、rational 与 reason；return 经法语出自拉丁语表示「转」的词。

items.example: The rate rose to five percent.
Interest rates moved higher.
The ratio of debt to income matters.
items.exampleCN: 债务与收入的比率很重要。

items.example: The ration was cut in wartime.
They made a rational choice.

items.meaning: the power to think, or a cause
items.example: She gave a clear reason.

items.meaning: able to be assessed or taxed
items.example: The land is rateable property.

items.exampleCN: 他们按十天比例分摊了房租。

items.example: The return exceeded the cost.

senses.title: Held as a prisoner
senses.definition: kept in a place and not allowed to leave, as a prisoner or a caged animal
senses.definitionCN: 被关在某处不许离开，如俘虏或笼中动物
senses.example: The captive soldiers were marched inland.
senses.exampleCN: 被俘的士兵被押往内陆。
senses.why: From Latin captivus, taken from capere, to seize.
senses.whyCN: 源自拉丁语 captivus，词根 capere 意为抓取。

senses.title: Unable to leave a situation
senses.definition: forced to stay in a situation, such as an audience or a market
senses.definitionCN: 被迫留在某种处境中，如听众或市场
senses.example: The delay left us a captive audience in the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 延误让我们成了大厅里走不开的听众。
senses.why: Commercial and social uses extend the cage to any place a person cannot exit.
senses.whyCN: 商业与社会用法把「笼子」扩展到任何走不开的地方。

intro.en: Captive comes straight from Latin captivus, a prisoner, from capere, to seize.
intro.cn: captive 直接来自拉丁语 captivus（俘虏），词根 capere 意为抓取。

items.en: Capere means to seize.
items.cn: capere 意为抓取。

items.cn: 十四世纪英语指战俘。

items.en: A captive market is one with no choice.
items.cn: 二十世纪出现「受制市场」之说。

items.en: Captive covers people, animals and audiences.
items.cn: 现代涵盖人、动物与听众。

note.cn: 形近组共享 capt- 词根；近义组把被违背意愿扣留的人从囚犯排到被拘留者。

entries.definition: To catch and hold.
entries.definitionCN: 捕获。

entries.definition: To hold attention completely.
entries.definitionCN: 使着迷。

entries.definition: Quick to find small faults.
entries.definitionCN: 吹毛求疵的。

entries.definition: Someone kept in prison or by captors.
entries.definitionCN: 囚犯；俘虏。

entries.definition: Someone held to force another to act.
entries.definitionCN: 人质。

entries.definition: A person kept in a prison or hospital.
entries.definitionCN: 囚犯；住院者。

entries.definition: A person kept in custody.

normalIntro.en: A captive is someone a hand has closed around.
normalIntro.cn: captive 就是被一只手攥住的人。

normal.en: Capere means to seize.
normal.cn: capere 意为抓取。

normal.en: Captivus is the one seized.
normal.cn: captivus 就是被抓的人。

normal.en: A captive bird cannot leave.
normal.cn: 被关的鸟走不掉。

normal.en: A captive audience cannot either.
normal.cn: 走不开的听众也一样。

normal.en: The cage can be a room or a market.
normal.cn: 笼子可以是一间房或一个市场。

abstract.en: A door that only opens from outside.
abstract.cn: 只能从外面打开的门。

abstract.en: Wings folded by circumstance.
abstract.cn: 被处境折起的翅膀。

abstract.en: Staying because leaving is not offered.
abstract.cn: 因为没人提供离开而留下。

examples.en: The captive was released after two years.
examples.cn: 那名俘虏两年后获释。

examples.en: Zoo animals are captive by definition.
examples.cn: 动物园里的动物按定义就是被圈养的。

examples.en: The outage held the whole city captive to the radio.
examples.cn: 停电让全城只能守着收音机。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「开普提夫」——被人一提就带走，成了俘虏。

sensesIntro.en: The prisoner and the stuck audience are both held by something they did not choose.
sensesIntro.cn: 俘虏与走不开的听众都被自己没选择的东西困住了。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bird on a perch that has stopped trying the bars

branches.en: Soldiers marched inland.
branches.cn: 被押往内陆的士兵。

definition_zh: 肌肉的；肌肉发达的；强有力的；强硬的
definition_en: relating to muscles, or having well-developed muscles and great physical or forceful power
core_image: 手臂一弯，皮下那束绳索绷起来，轮廓清楚地顶出皮肤
scene: 泳池边，刚上岸的游泳运动员甩了甩水，背部的线条随着动作起伏： The swimmer's muscular back rippled as she pulled herself out of the pool.
sceneCN: 这里指「肌肉发达的」（第 2 个义项：体格健壮、肌肉线条明显）；句意为游泳运动员从池中撑起身体时，背部发达的肌肉随动作起伏。

pos.zh: 肌肉的；与肌肉有关的
肌肉发达的；强壮的；（政策、行动）强有力的

derivatives.zh: 肌肉；力量；强行挤入
肌肉发达；强健
以肌肉力量；强壮地
肌肉系统；肌群
神经肌肉的

senses.title: Relating to muscle tissue
senses.definition: concerning muscle as tissue or as an anatomical structure
senses.definitionCN: 关于作为组织或解剖结构的肌肉
senses.example: Muscular tissue responds to nerve signals within milliseconds.
senses.exampleCN: 肌肉组织能在几毫秒内对神经信号作出反应。
senses.why: The suffix -ar simply turns the noun muscle into an adjective of relation, with no added meaning.
senses.whyCN: 末尾表示关系的形容词后缀只是把表示肌肉的名词变成形容词，并未增加新义。

senses.title: Well developed physique
senses.titleCN: 肌肉发达的；体格健壮的
senses.definition: having large, clearly visible muscles and a strong build
senses.definitionCN: 肌肉大而显眼、体格强壮
senses.example: Years of rowing left him lean and muscular.
senses.exampleCN: 多年划船让他精瘦而肌肉发达。
senses.why: From relating to muscle comes the descriptive sense: a body in which muscle is prominent is called muscular.
senses.whyCN: 从「与肌肉有关」引申出描述义：肌肉突出的身体就被称作「肌肉发达的」。

senses.title: Produced by muscle
senses.titleCN: 由肌肉产生的（力量、动作）
senses.definition: done or produced by the action of muscles rather than by tools or machines
senses.definitionCN: 由肌肉动作而非工具或机器完成或产生的
senses.example: The crate was moved by muscular effort alone, with no machinery.
senses.exampleCN: 这只木箱完全靠人力搬动，没有使用机械。
senses.why: This sense names the source of the force: the effort is muscular because muscle is what supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 这一义指明力的来源：说某项努力是「肌肉用力」，是因为力由肌肉提供。

senses.title: Of the muscular system
senses.titleCN: 肌肉系统的（教材与解剖语境）
senses.definition: belonging to the body system formed by all the muscles working with the skeleton
senses.definitionCN: 属于由全部肌肉与骨骼共同构成的身体系统
senses.example: The muscular system works with the skeleton to produce movement.
senses.exampleCN: 肌肉系统与骨骼协同产生运动。
senses.why: In anatomy the adjective marks a whole system, so a single word stands for the entire set of muscles.
senses.whyCN: 在解剖学中这个形容词标记整个系统，于是一个词就代表全部肌肉。

senses.title: Muscle-wasting disease
senses.titleCN: 肌肉萎缩性疾病的（医学定语）
senses.definition: describing conditions in which muscle fibres gradually weaken and waste away
senses.definitionCN: 描述肌肉纤维逐渐衰弱、萎缩的病症
senses.example: Muscular dystrophy weakens the fibres that support the limbs.
senses.exampleCN: 肌营养不良症使支撑肢体的肌肉纤维变弱。
senses.why: Here the adjective points to what the disease attacks, so the word identifies the tissue at risk rather than a healthy build.
senses.whyCN: 这里的形容词指出疾病攻击的对象，因此它标识的是受损组织，而非健康体格。

senses.title: Forceful writing or argument
senses.definition: vigorous, direct and hard to resist, said of style or reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 有力、直接、难以反驳，用于描述文风或论证
senses.example: The essay makes a muscular case for public transport.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章为公共交通提出了强有力的论证。
senses.why: Physical power is transferred to prose: an argument that pushes hard is imagined as having muscles.
senses.whyCN: 身体力量被转到文章上：推得很猛的论证被想象为长了肌肉。

senses.title: Aggressive policy
senses.definition: tough and assertive, willing to use pressure rather than persuasion
senses.definitionCN: 强硬而自信，宁用压力而非说服
senses.example: The government took a muscular approach to border control.
senses.exampleCN: 政府对边境管控采取了强硬做法。
senses.why: The metaphor is of a state flexing its muscles, so a muscular policy is one that shows force instead of arguing.
senses.whyCN: 比喻的起点是国家绷起肌肉，因此用于政策时，它指亮出力量而不靠说理。

senses.title: Demanding physical labour
senses.definition: requiring heavy bodily effort and strength
senses.definitionCN: 需要大量体力与力量的
senses.example: Farming here is muscular work, done mostly by hand.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的农活是体力活，大多靠手完成。
senses.why: Work is classified by the part of the body it uses, so a job that relies on strength is called muscular.
senses.whyCN: 工作按所使用的身体部位分类，因此靠力气干的活被称为「需要体力的」。

intro.en: Muscular is muscle plus the Latin relational suffix -aris, which English took as -ar. The word first described anatomy and only later a strong build. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: muscular 由 muscle 加拉丁关系后缀 -aris（英语作 -ar）构成。这个词先用于解剖描述，后来才指健壮的体格。年代均为约数。

items.en: The base is Latin musculus, a diminutive of mus mouse, used by Roman writers for the moving flesh of the body.
items.cn: 词基是拉丁 musculus，为 mus「老鼠」的指小形式，罗马作家用它指身体中会鼓动的肉。

items.en: The suffix -aris formed adjectives of relation, as in militaris and popularis; it marks belonging rather than resemblance.
items.cn: 后缀 -aris 构成表示关系的形容词，如 militaris、popularis；它标记「属于」而非「相似」。

items.en: Medical Latin used muscularis for structures made of or belonging to muscle, and the adjective passed into English anatomy.
items.cn: 医学拉丁语用 muscularis 指由肌肉构成或属于肌肉的结构，这一形容词随后进入英语解剖学。

items.en: English records muscular in anatomical writing; the first citation date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在解剖学文献中记录了 muscular，确切的最早书证年代存疑。

items.en: The descriptive sense of a strong, well-built body developed later, when muscle became a mark of health and training.
items.cn: 指体格强壮、肌肉发达的描述义出现较晚，是在肌肉成为健康与训练标志之后。

items.en: The figurative senses of forceful argument and aggressive policy belong to nineteenth- and twentieth-century political and literary writing.
items.cn: 指有力论证与强硬政策的比喻义，属于 19 至 20 世纪的政治与文学写作。

note.en: The first group holds forms built on the same stem; the second holds adjectives that also mean strong but from a different angle.
note.cn: 第一组是同词干构成的形式；第二组是同样表示强壮、但角度不同的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun that muscular describes; using it as an adjective is a common error.
entries.definitionCN: muscular 所描述的名词；把它当形容词用是常见错误。

entries.definition: The entire set of muscles, not a quality; muscular describes, musculature names the set.
entries.definitionCN: 全部肌肉的集合，不是性质；muscular 描述性质，musculature 命名集合。

entries.definition: The adverb of muscular, used of how something is done, not of what something is.
entries.definitionCN: muscular 的副词形式，说明做事方式，而非描述事物性质。

entries.definition: A shellfish whose name sounds like muscle but has nothing to do with muscle fibres.
entries.definitionCN: 一种贝类，名称读音像 muscle，却与肌肉纤维毫无关系。

entries.definition: Fit and trained for sport; it stresses performance rather than the visible size of muscles.
entries.definitionCN: 健康且受过运动训练的；强调运动表现而非肌肉的体积。

entries.definition: Big and strong in a heavy way; muscular can be lean, while brawny suggests bulk.
entries.definitionCN: 魁梧有力；muscular 可以指精瘦有肌肉，brawny 则暗示块头大。

entries.definition: Lean and tough, with visible cords; it stresses wiry strength rather than muscle mass.
entries.definitionCN: 精瘦结实、筋腱明显；强调筋劲而非肌肉量。

entries.definition: The general adjective for power of any kind; muscular is the specific bodily and figurative form.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何力量的形容词；muscular 是具体的身体义与比喻义形式。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real suffix, a real base noun and real medical collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的后缀、真实的名词词基与真实的医学搭配。

normal.en: muscle + -ar: the suffix means relating to, so muscular is the adjective of muscle.
normal.cn: muscle + -ar：后缀表示「与……有关」，因此 muscular 就是 muscle 的形容词。

normal.en: Musculature is the whole set, muscularity is the quality, and muscular is the describing word.
normal.cn: musculature 指整套肌肉，muscularity 指发达程度，muscular 则是描述词。

normal.en: Muscular dystrophy is the fixed medical phrase; the adjective marks the tissue the disease attacks.
normal.cn: muscular dystrophy 是固定医学短语；形容词标记疾病所攻击的组织。

normal.en: The word repeats in muscular system, muscular strength and muscular endurance, all anatomy or training contexts.
normal.cn: 这个词反复出现在 muscular system、muscular strength、muscular endurance，都是解剖或训练语境。

normal.en: Political writing uses a muscular case or a muscular policy when force replaces argument.
normal.cn: 政治写作在用力代替说理时，用 a muscular case 或 a muscular policy。

abstract.en: Picture a rope pulled tight under the skin, drawing a clear line where there was only a curve.
abstract.cn: 想象皮下有一根绳被拉紧，在原本只有曲线的地方画出一条清晰的线。

abstract.en: Picture an argument that pushes a door open instead of knocking politely.
abstract.cn: 想象一个论证直接把门推开，而不是礼貌地敲门。

abstract.en: Picture a state rolling up its sleeve: that gesture is what a muscular policy copies.
abstract.cn: 想象一个国家卷起袖子：强硬政策模仿的正是这个动作。

examples.en: Muscular endurance matters more than raw strength in long-distance swimming.
examples.cn: 在长距离游泳中，肌肉耐力比单纯的力气更重要。

examples.en: The muscular wall of the artery can narrow the channel.
examples.cn: 动脉的肌肉壁能够使管道变窄。

examples.en: His muscular prose leaves little room for doubt.
examples.cn: 他强有力的文笔几乎不留质疑的余地。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马搜了」（muscular）——马搜过全身，看哪里肌肉最发达 → 肌肉发达的

root: muscle + 拉丁关系后缀 -aris（英语 -ar）；词基为拉丁 musculus「小老鼠」，指小后缀 -culus。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from plain relation to visible build, to force, to whole system, to disease, and then out of the body into prose and policy.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从单纯的关系义，到可见的体格，到力量，到整个系统，到疾病，再走出身体进入文章与政策。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tightened cord under the skin that turns a soft outline into a hard line.
core.cn: 核心意象：皮下绷紧的绳索，把柔软的轮廓变成硬朗的线条。

branches.en: RELATION: the adjective points to tissue, then to the entire system built from it.
branches.cn: 关系：形容词先指组织，再指由该组织构成的整个系统。

branches.en: VISIBLE POWER: a body with prominent muscle, and effort supplied by muscle.
branches.cn: 可见的力量：肌肉突出的身体，以及由肌肉提供的力。

branches.en: FAILURE OF TISSUE: the same adjective marks the disease that wastes the fibres.
branches.cn: 组织的失效：同一个形容词标记使纤维萎缩的疾病。

branches.en: POWER OUTSIDE THE BODY: an argument that pushes, a policy that shows force.
branches.cn: 身体之外的力量：推得动的论证，亮出力量的政策。

branches.en: WORK CLASSIFIED BY BODY: a job is muscular when strength is the main tool.
branches.cn: 按身体分类的工作：当力气是主要工具时，这份工作就是「肌肉型」的。

intro.en: Muscular is the clearest example of the -ar suffix in this family: a noun becomes a relational adjective with no change of meaning.
intro.cn: muscular 是这一词族中 -ar 后缀最清楚的例子：名词变成关系形容词，词义不变。

latinIntro.en: Latin -alis and -aris both formed relational adjectives, and English inherited both as -al and -ar; muscular, vascular and similar follow the -aris line.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 -alis 与 -aris 都构成关系形容词，英语分别继承为 -al 与 -ar；muscular、vascular 等走的是 -aris 一线。

items.example: The muscle tightened under his hand.
items.exampleCN: 那块肌肉在他手下绷紧。

items.example: The suffix turns a noun into a describing word.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成描述词。

items.example: Muscular endurance improves with training.
The scan measured his muscularity.
items.exampleCN: 扫描测出了他的肌肉发达程度。

items.example: He lifted the beam muscularly, without a crane.
items.exampleCN: 他靠肌肉力量抬起横梁，没有用吊车。

items.example: Her musculature showed years of climbing.
items.exampleCN: 她的肌肉系统显出多年攀爬的痕迹。

items.meaning: relating to nerves and muscles together
items.meaningCN: 神经与肌肉共同相关的
items.example: Neuromuscular signals control the hand.
items.exampleCN: 神经肌肉信号控制手部。

items.example: The drug is given intramuscularly.
items.exampleCN: 这种药通过肌肉注射给药。

items.meaning: a genetic condition that wastes muscle
items.meaningCN: 使肌肉萎缩的遗传性疾病
items.example: Muscular dystrophy affects the fibres of the limbs.
items.exampleCN: 肌营养不良症影响四肢的肌肉纤维。

definition_zh: v. 使凸出；压凸；以浮雕装饰；压印（凸字）
definition_en: to decorate a surface with a design that stands out in relief
core_image: 一张厚纸被钢模压过，纸面鼓起一行字母，指尖摸过去能读出凸起，背面却是凹进去的
scene: 印厂的钢模合拢又打开，一张厚纸被压过，纸面鼓起一行字母，指尖摸过去能读出凸起。 The press embossed the title in raised letters on the cover.
sceneCN: 这里 emboss 指「压印凸字」（第 2 个义项：把字母压成凸起以便触摸）；句意是压印机在封面上把书名压成凸字。

pos.zh: 使凸出；压凸；浮雕装饰；压印

derivatives.zh: 凸饰；圆形浮雕
凸纹；浮雕装饰
压凸器；压印机

senses.title: To raise a design
senses.definition: to make a design stand out from a surface
senses.definitionCN: （动词）让纹样从表面凸出来
senses.example: They embossed the invitation with a gold border.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在请柬上压出一圈金色凸边。
senses.why: A steel die closing on thick paper until a line of letters rises on the face
senses.whyCN: 钢模在厚纸上合拢，直到纸面鼓起一行字母

senses.title: To print raised letters
senses.definition: to print letters in relief so that they can be read by touch
senses.definitionCN: （动词）把字母压成凸起，以便用指尖阅读
senses.example: The card was embossed so that a blind reader could feel the name.
senses.exampleCN: 卡片被压成凸字，好让盲人读者摸出名字。
senses.why: A fingertip reading a bump before the eye reads any ink
senses.whyCN: 指尖先摸到凸起，眼睛才读到油墨

senses.title: To ornament metal or leather
senses.definition: to ornament metal or leather with raised work
senses.definitionCN: （动词）用凸起的纹样装饰金属或皮革
senses.example: The binder embossed the leather with a pattern of vines.
senses.exampleCN: 装订工在皮革上压出藤纹图案。
senses.why: A leather cover pressed with a vine pattern that can be felt
senses.whyCN: 皮革封面被压出一圈能摸到的藤纹

intro.en: Emboss is em- plus boss, from Old French boce meaning a swelling or a bump; to emboss is to make bumps stand out on a surface.
intro.cn: emboss 由 em- 加 boss 组成，boss 来自古法语 boce（隆起；鼓包）；emboss 就是让鼓包在表面上凸出来。

items.en: Boce means a swelling or a bump, and gives English boss in its older sense.
items.cn: boce 意为隆起或鼓包，给出英语 boss 的较早意义。

items.en: Boce is used for a rounded ornament on a shield or a ceiling.
items.cn: boce 用于指盾牌或天花板上的圆形凸饰。

items.en: Emboss appears in the 1300s, meaning to ornament with raised work.
items.cn: emboss 出现于 14 世纪，意为用凸起的纹样装饰。

items.en: Embossed is used for leather and metal pressed with a pattern.
items.cn: embossed 用于指压出纹样的皮革与金属。

items.en: Embossing becomes an industrial process for paper and book covers.
items.cn: 压凸成为纸张与书封的工业工序。

items.en: Emboss is used for printing raised dots that can be read by touch.

dict_mnemonic.text: emboss ＝ em-（使进入）＋ boss（凸饰；鼓包，古法语 boce）＝「让鼓包凸出来」。三单 embosses，过去式与过去分词 embossed，现在分词 embossing；名词 embossment 凸纹装饰，工具名 embosser 压凸器；同根 boss 在建筑里指圆形凸饰，不是老板那个义项。三类用法：压凸图案 emboss a pattern 压出图案、emboss a logo 压出标志；凸字 embossed in gold 烫金凸字、embossed paper 压纹纸、embossed Braille 凸点盲文；皮革金属 embossed leather 压花皮革。形容词 embossed 最常见：an embossed cover 压凸封面。近义 engrave 是刻进去（凹），imprint 与 stamp 是压上标记，不一定凸起；emboss 的关键是凸出来、摸得到，与 deboss（压凹）正好相反。
