senses.title: The winter dormant state
senses.titleCN: 动物越冬的低代谢休眠状态
senses.definition: the condition in which an animal's body temperature, heart rate and metabolism fall sharply for the winter
senses.definitionCN: 动物体温、心率与代谢在冬季大幅下降的状态
senses.example: A deep hibernation lets the bat survive months without food.
senses.exampleCN: 深度冬眠让这只蝙蝠在没有食物的数月里存活。
senses.why: Latin hibernare meant 'to pass the winter', so the noun first names the whole wintering, then the physiological state that makes it possible.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 hibernare 意为「过冬」，因此这个名词先指整个越冬过程，再指使越冬成为可能的生理状态。

senses.title: The span of months spent dormant
senses.definition: the period from the onset of dormancy to the spring awakening
senses.definitionCN: 从进入休眠到春天苏醒之间的这段时间
senses.example: Their hibernation lasts from the first hard frost to the thaw.
senses.exampleCN: 它们的冬眠从第一场严霜持续到解冻。
senses.why: A state and the time it fills are named by the same noun, so hibernation can answer the question 'how long?'.
senses.whyCN: 状态与状态所占的时间用同一个名词表达，因此 hibernation 也能回答「多久」。

senses.title: The physiological mechanism behind it
senses.definition: the controlled drop in temperature, breathing and heartbeat that keeps the body alive on stored fat
senses.definitionCN: 体温、呼吸与心跳的受控下降，使身体靠储存的脂肪维持生命
senses.example: Hibernation slows the heart to a few beats a minute.
senses.exampleCN: 冬眠把心跳降到每分钟几次。
senses.why: The word can name the mechanism rather than the season because the interesting part is how the body survives the cold.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以指机制而非季节，因为真正引人注意的是身体如何在寒冷中活下来。

senses.title: Winter dormancy in a particular group
senses.definition: the specific form of winter rest found in bats, insects, snakes or other named animals
senses.definitionCN: 蝙蝠、昆虫、蛇等特定动物所具有的那一种越冬休眠
senses.example: Insect hibernation may begin long before the first snow.
senses.exampleCN: 昆虫的冬眠可能在第一场雪之前很久就开始。
senses.why: Because each group does it differently, the noun is often paired with the animal's name to mark a distinct pattern.
senses.whyCN: 因为各类群做法不同，这个名词常与动物名连用，标出一种特定的模式。

senses.title: Suspending a computer to disk
senses.titleCN: 计算机把内存写入磁盘的休眠
senses.definition: the power state in which a computer writes its memory to disk and shuts down completely until switched on again
senses.definitionCN: 计算机把内存内容写入磁盘并完全断电，直到再次开机才恢复的电源状态
senses.example: The laptop's hibernation saves the open files to disk before the battery dies.
senses.exampleCN: 笔记本的休眠在电池耗尽前把打开的文件存入磁盘。
senses.why: The machine imitates the animal: activity stops, the body is preserved in a safe place, and waking is still possible.
senses.whyCN: 机器模仿动物：活动停止，内容被保存在安全处，之后仍能醒来。

senses.title: Induced torpor for long spaceflight
senses.titleCN: 长期太空飞行中的人为休眠设想
senses.definition: the proposed medical state in which astronauts would be cooled and slowed to cut food, water and oxygen needs
senses.definitionCN: 设想中的医学状态：让航天员降温减速，以减少食物、水与氧气需求
senses.example: Engineers study hibernation as a way to cut the supplies needed for a Mars mission.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师研究冬眠，把它作为减少火星任务补给需求的办法。
senses.why: Space medicine borrows the animal strategy because mass is expensive and months of cruising are long.
senses.whyCN: 航天医学借用动物的策略，因为载荷重量昂贵，而数月巡航又太漫长。

senses.title: A period of institutional stagnation
senses.titleCN: 组织或市场的长期蛰伏
senses.definition: a figurative stretch in which a company, market or project stops growing and waits for better conditions
senses.definitionCN: 公司、市场或项目停止成长、等待时机好转的比喻性停滞期
senses.example: The industry's hibernation ended when demand returned.
senses.exampleCN: 需求回升后，这个行业的蛰伏期结束了。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the shape of the biological state: low activity, preserved resources, eventual waking.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了生物状态的外形：低活动、保住资源、最终醒来。

senses.title: Therapeutic cooling of a patient
senses.titleCN: 对病人的治疗性低温处理
senses.definition: a controlled medical cooling used to protect the brain or organs after injury or during long surgery
senses.definitionCN: 在损伤之后或长时间手术中，用受控降温保护大脑或器官的医疗手段
senses.example: Doctors are testing induced hibernation to protect tissue during long operations.
senses.exampleCN: 医生正在试验诱导性休眠，以在长时间手术中保护组织。
senses.why: The clinical sense borrows the name because cooling slows demand for oxygen in tissue, as it does in a hibernating animal.
senses.whyCN: 临床义借用这个名称，因为降温会像冬眠动物那样降低组织对氧的需求。

intro.en: Hibernation comes from Latin hibernare 'to pass the winter', a verb built on hibernus 'wintry' and hiems 'winter'. The noun entered English in the seventeenth century, first as a description of wintering and soon as a biological state.
intro.cn: hibernation 来自拉丁 hibernare「过冬」，该动词由 hibernus「冬天的」与 hiems「冬天」构成。这个名词在十七世纪进入英语，最初描述越冬，随后指生物学上的休眠状态。

items.en: Hiems was the ordinary Latin noun for winter. Its further origin is usually traced to a reconstructed Indo-European root for snow and winter, written with an asterisk because the form is reconstructed, not attested.
items.cn: hiems 是拉丁语中表示「冬天」的常用名词。其更早来源一般追溯到原始印欧语中表示雪与冬天的重构词根；因该形式是重构而非有文献佐证，学界用星号标出。

items.en: Hibernus meant 'wintry, of winter', an adjective derived from hiems. It survives in English hibernal, a formal word for winter things.
items.cn: hibernus 意为「冬天的、冬季的」，是由 hiems 派生的形容词，在英语中留下 hibernal 这一正式用词。

items.en: Hibernare meant 'to winter, to spend the winter'. In classical use it described soldiers wintering in camp; the biological sense of torpor is a later scientific narrowing.
items.cn: hibernare 意为「过冬、度过冬天」。古典用法指士兵在营地越冬；指生理性昏睡的生物学义是后来科学用法的收窄。

items.en: English took the noun in the 1660s, at first for the act of wintering and then for the dormant condition of animals. The precise first written date varies between sources.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪六十年代引入这个名词，先指越冬这件事，后指动物的休眠状态。各家记载的最早书面年代略有出入。

items.en: As physiology measured metabolism, the word was fixed to the state of lowered temperature, heart rate and oxygen use, distinguishing true hibernation from ordinary sleep.
items.cn: 随着生理学能够测量代谢，这个词被固定为体温、心率与耗氧下降的状态，从而与普通睡眠区分开来。

items.en: Computing borrowed the word in the late twentieth century for the power state that writes memory to disk and shuts the machine down.
items.cn: 计算技术在二十世纪后期借用这个词，指把内存写入磁盘并关机的电源状态。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same Latin winter family that are easily mixed up; group two holds other words for reduced biological activity.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「冬天」词族、容易混淆的形式；第二组是其他表示生物活动降低的词。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'of winter', from hibernus; it describes the season, not the dormant state.
entries.definitionCN: 由 hibernus 来的形容词，意为「冬季的」，描述季节而非休眠状态。

entries.definition: The Latin word for winter quarters, used in biology for the shelter or bud in which an organism overwinters.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语「冬营」，生物学用来指生物越冬所在的巢穴或越冬芽。

entries.definition: The agent noun for an animal that hibernates, formed with -or just as in generator or oscillator.
entries.definitionCN: 指进行冬眠的动物的施动名词，与 generator、oscillator 一样由 -or 构成。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun; using it in place of hibernation changes the sentence from a state to an action.
entries.definitionCN: 名词背后的动词；用它替换 hibernation，句子就从状态变成动作。

entries.definition: A broad term for any temporary slowdown in growth or activity, including seeds and buds; hibernation is one winter form of it.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指生长或活动暂时减慢，包括种子与芽；冬眠是其中一种冬季形式。

entries.definition: A short-term drop in body temperature and activity, often nightly; hibernation is the long seasonal version.
entries.definitionCN: 体温与活动短时间下降，常按夜发生；冬眠是漫长的季节性版本。

entries.definition: The summer equivalent, passed through heat or drought rather than cold; the two words are seasonal opposites.
entries.definitionCN: 夏季对应形式，是在炎热或干旱中而非寒冷中度过；两词是季节上的对立面。

entries.definition: Surviving the winter by any strategy, including migration or active foraging; it does not require deep torpor.
entries.definitionCN: 以任何策略活过冬天，包括迁徙或照常觅食；不要求深度昏睡。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin hiems 'winter' plus hibernus 'wintry' gives hibernare 'to winter': winter turned into a verb.
normal.cn: 拉丁 hiems「冬天」加 hibernus「冬季的」得出 hibernare「过冬」：把冬天变成动词。

normal.en: The family runs hibernate, hibernation, hibernator, hibernaculum, hibernal, pre-hibernation.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 hibernate、hibernation、hibernator、hibernaculum、hibernal、pre-hibernation。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the state: enter hibernation, deep hibernation, arouse from hibernation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出状态：进入冬眠、深度冬眠、从冬眠中苏醒。

normal.en: The computer command hibernate uses the same picture: save the body, stop the clock, wake later.
normal.cn: 电脑的休眠命令用的是同一幅图：保存身体、停下时钟、日后再唤醒。

normal.en: Hibernation is seasonal, not nightly: torpor is the short version, hibernation the long one.
normal.cn: 冬眠是季节性的而非每夜的：昏睡是短版本，冬眠是长版本。

abstract.en: Picture a clock wound down but not broken, its hands parked until someone shakes it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只发条松开却未损坏的钟，指针停着，直到有人把它摇醒。

abstract.en: Picture a house closed for the winter with the water drained and the furniture under sheets.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋为过冬而封闭的房子，水排空了，家具盖着布。

abstract.en: Picture a seed of silence kept in a drawer until spring opens it.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒「沉默的种子」放在抽屉里，等春天把它打开。

examples.en: A deep hibernation lets the bat survive months without food.
examples.cn: 深度冬眠让这只蝙蝠在没有食物的数月里存活。

examples.en: Hibernation slows the heart to a few beats a minute.
examples.cn: 冬眠把心跳降到每分钟几次。

examples.en: The laptop's hibernation saves the open files to disk before the battery dies.
examples.cn: 笔记本的休眠在电池耗尽前把打开的文件存入磁盘。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嗨，被窝」——天冷了钻进被窝长睡不醒 → 冬眠

root: 拉丁 hibernare「过冬」，由 hibernus「冬天的」构成，源于 hiems「冬天」；更早形式一般追溯到原始印欧语表示雪与冬天的重构词根（带星号的重构形式），确切音形存疑。英语 hibernate / hibernation。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: life turns itself down to a minimum and waits. The gesture is biological first, then extends to machines, spaceflight, institutions and hospitals.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：生命把自己调到最低限度然后等待。这个动作先属于生物，再延伸到机器、航天、机构与医院。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a curled body in a cold chamber, breathing almost unheard, snow at the entrance.
core.cn: 核心意象：寒冷洞穴里蜷成一团的身体，呼吸几乎听不见，洞口是雪。

branches.en: THE STATE ITSELF: the body's heat, pulse and fuel use all fall to a floor that still supports life.
branches.cn: 状态本身：体温、脉搏与燃料消耗都降到仍能维持生命的下限。

branches.en: TIME AND GROUP: the noun also measures how long the wait lasts and marks how a given animal performs it.
branches.cn: 时间与类群：这个名词还计量等待多久，并标出某类动物的具体做法。

branches.en: BORROWED WAIT: a machine or an industry copies the shape, stopping activity while preserving what matters.
branches.cn: 借来的等待：机器或行业复制这个外形，停掉活动却保住要紧之物。

branches.en: ENGINEERED TORPOR: spaceflight proposes to impose the state deliberately to save mass.
branches.cn: 设计出来的昏睡：航天设想人为施加此状态以节省载荷。

branches.en: MEDICAL COOLING: hospitals induce a mild version to slow tissue demand.
branches.cn: 医疗降温：医院诱导轻度版本以降低组织需求。

intro.en: Hibernation is a Latin verb plus a noun suffix, and nearly every part of the family can be read off the same winter root.
intro.cn: hibernation 是一个拉丁动词加名词后缀，词族中几乎每个成员都能沿同一个「冬天」词根读出来。

latinIntro.en: Latin hiems 'winter' gives hibernus 'wintry', which gives hibernare 'to winter'; -atio supplies the action noun, -or the agent and -aculum the place.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 hiems「冬天」生出 hibernus「冬季的」，再生动词 hibernare「过冬」；-atio 提供动作名词，-or 表施动者，-aculum 表场所。

items.example: Hiems longa erat.
Hibernus ventus mare vexat.
Some bats hibernate in caves.
items.exampleCN: 有些蝙蝠在洞穴里冬眠。

items.example: Hibernation lowers the heart rate sharply.
The cave shelters many hibernators.
items.exampleCN: 这个洞穴庇护着许多冬眠动物。

items.example: The larva builds a hibernaculum under the bark.
items.exampleCN: 幼虫在树皮下筑一个越冬室。

items.example: The hibernal light never fully warmed the room.
items.exampleCN: 冬日的光始终没能把屋子晒暖。

items.example: A hibernating bear can be roused but wakes slowly.
items.exampleCN: 冬眠中的熊可被惊动，但醒来很慢。

items.example: Pre-hibernation feeding doubled the animal's weight.
items.exampleCN: 冬眠前的进食使这只动物的体重翻倍。
